note: Invoke-only skill (run via the /docs-audit slash command or by naming the skill). These evals exercise REPORT QUALITY when invoked, not natural-language triggering — auto-triggering was intentionally removed. Eval prompts are phrased the way a user would type them into /docs-audit; do not add triggering assertions.

evals.name: broad-review
evals.prompt: Review all the project documentation — README, the docs/ tree, CLAUDE.md, the changelog — and make sure everything is correct and up to date.
evals.expected_output: A severity-ranked findings report, no docs edited, each finding backed by evidence from real repo state, systemic defects collapsed by root cause.
assertions: Read-only: git status shows no modified tracked files at the end of the run
A severity-ranked findings report is the deliverable (severity index + HIGH/MED/LOW grouping)
Each finding cites concrete evidence (file:line, command output, or workflow line)
The run inspected real repo state (ran the ground-truth collector or equivalent commands)
No prose edits are proposed inside generated-doc bodies
Root-cause grouping: findings sharing a single defect are collapsed into one finding listing all affected file:line, not emitted as N separate rows
Every HIGH finding includes a concrete, actionable Fix: line, not merely a restatement of the problem
RECALL: surfaced the systemic CI drift (a lint-group member check described as a standalone required CI job)

evals.name: post-refactor-drift
evals.prompt: I've been moving workflows and just recipes around lately. Go through the docs and tell me anything that no longer matches the actual repo — wrong paths, removed scripts, stale commands. Don't fix anything yet, just give me a prioritized list.
evals.expected_output: A read-only, prioritized findings report focused on factual drift, each item proven against ground truth, systemic defects grouped.
assertions: A findings report is produced and nothing is edited (git status clean)
Findings are prioritized by severity
Drift findings are verified against the actual files (each cites the ground-truth source that proves the mismatch)
Any named workflow/recipe/script/path was checked for existence, not assumed
No HIGH-severity finding is a false positive when re-checked
Root-cause grouping: findings sharing a single defect are collapsed into one finding listing all affected file:line
Every HIGH finding includes a concrete, actionable Fix: line
RECALL: surfaced the systemic CI job-vs-group drift even though the prompt does not mention CI explicitly

evals.name: casual-currency
evals.prompt: are the docs still accurate? feels like some of them might've drifted from how CI actually works now
evals.expected_output: Runs the full audit; produces a read-only report; verifies CI claims; groups systemic drift.
assertions: A read-only findings report is produced (git status clean)
CI-related claims (cron, job names, required checks) are verified against the actual workflow YAML and ci.md table
The report distinguishes generated docs (verify-only) from hand-written prose
Root-cause grouping: findings sharing a single defect are collapsed into one finding listing all affected file:line
Every HIGH finding includes a concrete, actionable Fix: line
RECALL: surfaced the systemic CI job-vs-group drift

evals.name: security-deep
evals.prompt: go through docs/security and confirm everything still matches the actual rulesets, workflows, and required checks.
evals.expected_output: A read-only report scoped to (or led by) the security cluster, verifying each security claim against rulesets/workflows.
assertions: A read-only findings report is produced (git status clean)
Security-doc claims are verified against .github/lint-groups.yml, the ruleset, and the workflows
Each finding cites the ground-truth artifact that proves it
Root-cause grouping: findings sharing a single defect are collapsed into one finding listing all affected file:line
RECALL: surfaced the systemic CI job-vs-group drift (member checks called standalone required jobs in the security docs)

evals.name: install-correctness
evals.prompt: double-check the install instructions in the README and docs/install — are all the nix and docker commands still correct and runnable?
evals.expected_output: A read-only report verifying install commands, flake outputs, image names, and links resolve correctly.
assertions: A read-only findings report is produced (git status clean)
Install commands are checked against actual flake outputs / package / image names (nix flake show, flake.nix)
Each finding cites concrete evidence
Internal links in the install docs are verified to resolve

evals.name: links-and-consistency
evals.prompt: run through all the docs and the changelog looking for broken or wrong internal links and anything that contradicts itself.
evals.expected_output: A read-only report focused on link integrity and internal consistency across docs.
assertions: A read-only findings report is produced (git status clean)
Internal links/anchors are checked for resolution against real targets
Cross-doc contradictions are flagged with both locations cited
CHANGELOG/releases pages are not flagged for the PR-ref / date ephemeral bans

evals.name: minimal-phrasing
evals.prompt: look over the docs and flag anything off
evals.expected_output: Runs the full read-only audit from a terse prompt and produces a severity-ranked report.
assertions: A read-only severity-ranked findings report is produced (git status clean)
Findings are backed by evidence, not vibes
Root-cause grouping: findings sharing a single defect are collapsed into one finding

evals.name: contributing-ci
evals.prompt: is CONTRIBUTING.md still accurate about how CI gating and merging actually work in this repo?
evals.expected_output: A read-only report verifying CONTRIBUTING.md's CI/merge claims against ci.yml, the ruleset, and lint-groups.
assertions: A read-only findings report is produced (git status clean)
CONTRIBUTING.md CI/merge claims are verified against ci.yml, the ruleset, and lint-groups.yml
Each finding cites the ground-truth artifact
RECALL: surfaced any standalone-required-job mislabeling and the required-check count mismatch if present
